g.text: - a deterministic authorization gate for AI-to-AI commerce
LLMs propose. Policies constrain. A deterministic verifier authorizes.
Nothing probabilistic can widen authority. The agent cannot overspend.
1 A legitimate purchase clears the gate
intent Buy running shoes under ₹5,000 with 30-day returns, automatically
(signed by the issuer, not the agent)
bounded negotiation, one round, two hard walls (buyer cap and seller floor):
2 Tamper one field of the receipt - the signature breaks
the cryptography is real, not decorative
3 Nine attack classes, nine machine-readable reason codes
all nine blocked with the correct reason code:
4 The audit log is hash-chained - tampering is detectable
after editing one past entry: intact
-> first break at seq 1 (entry_hash does not match pa
5 The honest scoreboard - computed live, nothing pre-written
(generating fresh adversarial + legitimate sets and running the gate...)
share still cleared by the gate 100.0%
(the risk classifier's precision/recall is reported separately by `make benchmark` -
a probabilistic model never shares a scoreboard with gate correctness.)
Autonomous commerce is not trustworthy because we say it is safe.
It is trustworthy because we can measure where it fails. That is BAZAAR.
